# ReixOS
# The QEMU boot matrix, as data. scripts/scenarios.sh reads this file and boots
# one row at a time through scripts/smoke.sh, so a new machine configuration is
# a new line here rather than a new script or a new Makefile target.
# Tab-separated, ten columns, `-` for a column that does not apply. Blank lines
# and `#` lines are ignored. A field may contain spaces; it may not contain a
# tab, and runs of tabs collapse, so every column needs its placeholder.
#   id         row name: its serial log lands in .reix/scenario-<id>.log
#   mem        guest RAM, e.g. `4M` (`-` = the machine default)
#   initrd     `qemu` (handed over with -initrd) or `embedded` (the copy the
#              plugin links into kernel.bin under `.initrd`)
#   flags      QEMU flags appended after the base set (`-` = none). Appended and
#              not merged: QEMU keeps the last `-cpu`/`-machine` it is given, so
#              a row overrides one of them without restating the whole machine.
#   mode       `verdict` stops the guest at the first success/failure marker,
#              exactly like `make smoke`. `window` keeps it running for the full
#              timeout and judges the log afterwards, which is what a row needs
#              when it asserts lines printed after the success marker.
#   timeout    seconds: the deadline under `verdict`, the run length under `window`
#   required   markers that must all appear, in this order, `|`-separated. The
#              order is a subsequence, not adjacency: other lines may sit
#              between two markers, and each marker only has to appear after
#              the line that satisfied the previous one.
#   forbidden  markers that must not appear anywhere, `|`-separated (`-` = none)
#   post       extra check run after the markers hold (`-` = none). The names are
#              the post_* functions in scripts/scenarios.sh.
#   expect     `pass`, `xfail:<reason>`, or `skip-if:<condition>`
# On the marker sets, both of which are deliberately narrow:
#   * A healthy boot prints no `[ ERROR ]` line at all, verified against every
#     configuration below, so the level tag itself is forbidden rather than any
#     particular message. A panic is caught twice: `[ PANIC ]` is the level tag
#     and `REIX-PANIC` is the report banner, which the nested-fault path prints
#     without a level tag.
#   * Only single-writer lines are required. The kernel's `[ INFO  ][ELF ]`
#     spawn lines interleave with userland output and shred whatever line they
#     land in the middle of, so nothing printed during a spawn is asserted -
#     including the initrd page-sharing line, which is the one that shreds.
# id
# The configuration `make smoke` boots: machine default RAM, initrd from QEMU.
# The required chain is one boot read end to end - the pre-Swift banner, the
# subsystems in bring-up order, the handoff to EL0, init, and finally the
# terminal server, which is the last thing init starts that announces itself.
default

column1: # A machine with no PMUv3 block. The PMUVer gate is supposed to make profiling
# optional, so the boot has to reach the same end state with the counters left
# alone; the forbidden line is the one the PMU prints when it does come up, and
# its absence is what says the gate closed instead of the boot getting lucky.
no-pmu

column1: # The guard on smoke-4m's coupling: at 4 MiB, MEM and INITRD_MODE are one knob
# and not two, because QEMU drops an -initrd halfway up RAM and then 2 MiB-aligns
# the generated DTB after it, which lands past the top of the machine. QEMU says
# exactly that and exits before the kernel runs, so its message is what this row
# requires and the success marker is what it forbids.
# Which makes this row failing good news rather than a regression: it would mean
# the guest booted all the way through on `qemu` at 4 MiB, INITRD_MODE=embedded
# stopped being load-bearing, and the coupling can be relaxed - in `smoke-4m` and
# `run-4m` in the Makefile, and in the mem-4m row above.
dtb-squeeze

column1: # The kernel's own account of the boot, cross-checked against the console's.
# Init dumps the trace ring ~800 ms after the children are done, which is later
# than the success marker, hence `window`; the post-check then decodes the same
# log with `swift package reix trace --boot` and asserts all eleven boot phases
# come out in TraceBootPhase order.
trace-boot

column1: # The disk, end to end and in one boot: the bus walker reads a device id off a
# transport, starts a driver for it, checks the sectors while it is still the
# only process that can reach them, and hands the whole disk to a file system
# that mounts it. Every line below is printed by a different process, and the
# order they appear in is the order the authority travelled.
# `window` and not `verdict` because all of it happens after the marker a
# verdict row stops on, and the disk is not asserted to be blank: a row that
# required the formatting line would pass once and fail on every run after,
# since the image outlives the boot on purpose.
storage
